title: Remember this is a business first.
body:
I had Finch when it first came out. I loved it and used it every day. 

When it became apparent that I did not require an electronic cheerleader anymore, I deleted the app. No hard feelings, it ran its course. 

A week ago, a friend asked me to join because she is having a hard time. I said ok! 

Imagine my surprise when I could no longer log in with my Apple ID. More than a year’s worth of progress and items were gone. 

I contacted costumer service and they apologised and said they could not help me log in but if I had a backup of the game, I was fine. 

What is the point of the plus membership if you lose everything when you uninstall? 

I never heard back from customer service. I started again but there is no way I am paying for things I already have. 

I do not mind paying developers to keep doing good work. But to ignore their paying base in favour of the MLM scheme (“Add More Friends!”) is more than dubious for those that are already mentally suffering. 

Finch is cute and dopamine rewarding. That is not the debate. Paying for virtual goods is a trust people put in you as a company. ✌🏽

title: Elisabeth
body: Finch has honestly become a big part of my everyday life. It’s such a great app! I just put all my main self-care routines in there and keep checking things off throughout the day- it’s so liberating! I tend to forget things, like drinking water or even eating sometimes, lol. But the stomach obviously lets you know when you’re hungry (by making that growling noise). However, your body doesn’t let you know immediately that you’ve forgotten to drink enough water, unless you pay attention to the colour of your pee - which, let’s face it, we sometimes forget during a busy day. So yeah. This is a great way to remind yourself to cover your most basic needs first, before all else. And I love how it’s almost “tamagotchi” like, a pet that loves you. I can’t have any pets right now, due to my living situation (rental), so this is a perfect way to still feel like you almost do have a pet, lol. I have a child, but that’s different. Pet owners who are also parents (to children) will know what I mean. Anyways, thanks for an amazing app! Keep up the good work 🫶🏼

title: Money
body: I really really really love finch, it’s one of my favourite apps. And it can help me get motivated for the day and I can reflect a story about how my day was. But there is something I find kinda stupid because some of the things cost money, like for an example basic hygiene goals, sleeping goals, exercise goals. And a lot of other things cost money too. I think it’s kinda bad that it costs money because it’s supposed to be a self care app. Hygiene and mental health care shouldn’t cost money. title: Best on the market
body:
This app has helped me so incredibly much!!

title: Highly recommend!
body: I love this app so much! Having a Finch friend to follow me on my journey motivates me to do the small things for myself everyday, and it’s a game changer for sure. I love that I can shop clothes for them and save up for items with every task that I do. It also invites me to share my thoughts and I’m encouraged to write more than I would have otherwise by the rewards in the app. It’s a clever format and the cutest design! The exercises are great to connect more to the breath and the body. I’d love for there to me more options for stretching and movement. But that doesn’t take away all the amazing things this app has done for me already after only three weeks. And there are enough exercises and tasks to go a long way. Highly recommend trying Finch🧡🥰

title: Best self help app I’ve tried.
body: I’ve only used it for a couple days so far, but I must say I really like it. It’s cute, it has lots of journeys and activities, and definitely a good choice for a self help app. I love that we can dress them up. I also love the inclusion of gender neutral pronouns. It gets a big plus for not having ads, and that it’s perfectly usable even without spending money. However, app developers also pay rent, and that’s where the subscription comes in. I’d say the monthly price is just within the limits of what I call affordable (coming from a disabled person that can’t afford these ridiculous two digit $ monthly or even weekly prices we see in many apps these days). The yearly price isn’t bad either, when it comes to being worth it. If I get enough extra that I can afford one year I might do it, as that’s definitely the better choice. I think it’s important to support those that make quality apps like this, but the fact that it’s very good even as a free app is absolutely great as there’s definitely many who needs this but can’t afford it. Me and my best friend both play and love this, and send each other good vibes multiple times a day. I also love the widget, it’s really nice. Would be nice with more size options (medium), but that’s such a minor thing that it doesn’t take anything away from the score. Honestly 10/10 app. Thank you for making this app, I really feel like it’ll help me get more control on my life and mental health.
